paragraphs.source_en:
(‘So gentle and so full of dignity my lady appears when she greets anyone that all tongues tremble and
fall silent and eyes dare not look at her. She goes on her way, hearing herself praised, graciously clothed
with humility; and seems a creature come down from heaven to earth to make the miraculous known.
 She appears so beautiful to those who gaze at her that through the eyes she sends a sweetness into
the heart such as none can understand but he who experiences it; and from her lips seems to come a
spirit, gentle and full of love, that says to the soul: “Sigh.” ’ Trans. F&B)
25. Cp. Adonais 480.

paragraphs.source_en:
In the Phaedrus beauty is described as the only one of the ideas which has a perfectly clear
and distinct image upon earth; . . . Emily . . . is the mirror which reflects most brightly the
glory of the unseen world. The beauty of her mind is far greater than the beauty of her body,
which is only its dim reflection; she is an image of the eternal beauty.
